# Publish via Buffer

**The normal route is a PR.** Use the `open-content-pr` skill: when the PR merges to main, GitHub Actions schedules everything in Buffer. This skill covers the **local CLI**, used for one-time setup (`channels --save`), for urgent one-off posts the user explicitly wants without a PR, and for debugging.

Script: `scripts/buffer.ts` (run it with `npm run buffer -- …`). There is **no `.env` file**: the key lives only as the GitHub secret `BUFFER_API_KEY`. For a rare local run, the user sets it for that terminal session only (PowerShell `$env:BUFFER_API_KEY="..."`). Never write the key to any file. Shared logic is in `scripts/lib/buffer-api.ts`. Without `--media-url`, the CLI uses the committed file from `output/<platform>/<slug>/` through its public jsDelivr URL (`scripts/lib/media-url.ts`). That file must be committed **and pushed** first; the CLI checks this.

## Facts that shape this workflow

- **API:** `https://api.buffer.com` (GraphQL, public beta). Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $BUFFER_API_KEY`. Create the key at https://publish.buffer.com/settings/api.
- **Supported here:** Instagram and Facebook, as feed post, reel or story. **Buffer does not support WhatsApp.** WhatsApp files stay in `output/whatsapp/<slug>/` for the user to share by hand (Status, Business catalogue or broadcast list).
- **Media must be a public, permanent https URL.** Buffer has no upload endpoint and fetches the file when it publishes. Signed or expiring links (S3 presigned, Google Drive or Dropbox share pages) fail silently. This repo is public, so committed files are served by jsDelivr pinned to a commit (permanent, correct content types, ≤ 20 MB per file). You can also pass your own `--media-url`.
- **Draft renders are blocked:** anything rendered with `--allow-lowres` or `--draft` is refused for real publishing (`draftOnly` in its manifest).
- **Rate limits (free plan):** 150 requests per 15 min. The script retries once on HTTP 429.
- **Known Buffer bugs:** Instagram `firstComment` may not save through the API, so check it in Buffer after scheduling. API-created reels can show the type "reel" instead of "reels" when edited in Buffer's UI.

## AI content label

The script **never** sends Buffer's `isAiGenerated` flag. It is only added if `--ai-disclosure` is passed explicitly, so the user's default is no AI label. Before publishing a **reel** made from photorealistic AI-generated people or scenes, mention once to the user that Meta's rules require disclosure for realistic AI video. Then follow their decision. Meta can also add its "AI info" label by its own detection, and Buffer has no control over that. Do not add steps whose purpose is to hide or strip AI provenance.

## Steps

### 0. One-time setup
1. Add the GitHub secret `BUFFER_API_KEY` (repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions).
2. GitHub → Actions → **List Buffer channels** → Run workflow. Copy the JSON from the run summary into `config/buffer-channels.json` and commit it via a PR (channel ids are not secret).

If the channel list shows `[QUEUE PAUSED]`, tell the user. Posts will sit in the queue until they unpause it in Buffer.

### 1. Pre-flight (all must pass)
- `npm run check:media -- output/instagram/<slug> output/facebook/<slug>` passes.
- `caption.txt` exists in each platform folder and the user has approved the captions.
- The creative was not rendered with `--allow-lowres`. Check `output/_masters/<slug>/manifest-*.json` warnings.
- Public URLs for the exact files to post: feed → `ig-feed.jpg`, story → `story.jpg`, reel → `reel.mp4`.

### 2. Dry run, show the user, then publish
```bash
# Feed post to the queue on both networks
npm run buffer -- post --slug <slug> --kind post --platforms instagram,facebook \
  --media-url https://cdn.example.com/<slug>/ig-feed.jpg --dry-run

# Reel at an exact time (IST shown; script converts to UTC)
npm run buffer -- post --slug <slug> --kind reel --platforms instagram,facebook \
  --media-url https://cdn.example.com/<slug>/reel.mp4 --at 2026-11-20T19:00:00+05:30

# Story, publish now
npm run buffer -- post --slug <slug> --kind story --platforms instagram \
  --media-url https://cdn.example.com/<slug>/story.jpg --now
```
Options: `--queue` (default: the next free slot in the Buffer schedule) · `--at <ISO datetime>` · `--now` · `--draft` (saves to Buffer drafts for review in the app) · `--first-comment "…"` · repeat `--media-url` for a multi-image feed post · `--thumb-offset <ms>` (reel cover; defaults to the value from `manifest-reel.json`).

Always run `--dry-run` first and show the user the platforms, kind, schedule and caption preview. **Publishing is outward-facing: get explicit confirmation** before running without `--dry-run`, unless the user has already said to post it.

### 3. After publishing
- Results are appended to `output/_masters/<slug>/publish-log.jsonl`.
- Tell the user the Buffer post ids and due times, and remind them of the WhatsApp files: `output/whatsapp/<slug>/`.

## Good posting times (India, IST) — defaults to suggest

Instagram: 11:00–13:00 and 19:00–21:30 · Facebook: 12:00–14:00 and 19:00–21:00 · WhatsApp Status: 09:00–10:00 and 19:00–20:00. Before festivals and the wedding season, post 7–10 days ahead.
